notes: p=0 ring construction is pure edge-list push — ~5.8-7.4 Melem/s,
edge-index assignment). Per-edge cost is roughly constant in size.
p=0.5 in the simple-graph regime costs ~3.5x more than the p=0
baseline at size=10_000: the dominant overhead is the HashSet of
canonical edge pairs (insert + lookup per rewire attempt) plus the
small probability of rejection on dense rewires.
The p-sweep at fixed size=1000, nei=4 shows the expected near-linear
scaling in p: 0.01 → 0.10 doubles cost (only one of the two rewire
passes does meaningful work), 0.10 → 1.0 increases by ~3x as both
passes rewire ~all endpoints and the HashSet hit rate climbs.
Multigraph fast path (loops=true, multiple=true) at size=10_000 with
p=0.5 runs at 3.91 Melem/s — ~2.5x faster than the simple-graph
equivalent (1.58 Melem/s) because the HashSet of canonical pairs is
skipped entirely. This validates the conditional-allocation design.
Validation/setup overhead is negligible at sizes ≥ 100. Construction
for size < 50 (not benched) is dominated by Graph::with_vertices().
